proposal_scope: Recurring propagation mechanism recovered from multiple OpenAI self-replicating prompt-injection occurrences. This file proposes a class boundary only; it does not modify the canonical taxonomy or retroactively classify any Incident.

proposed_class.name: Instruction-State Propagation Authority
proposed_class.plain_english: Copying instruction-bearing or control-capable content into a new carrier, context or recipient has its own authority boundary; replication must not silently preserve or extend its ability to govern later execution.
proposed_class.definition: The property by which instruction-bearing, policy-like, control-capable or otherwise execution-shaping material may be reproduced, reposted, persisted, forwarded or copied across a carrier, recipient, channel, file, context or execution boundary only where the propagation itself has an independently sufficient authority basis and preserves the material's applicable trust, provenance and non-authorising status. The class concerns the propagation step itself: downstream re-execution is not required where the reproduction materially preserves or extends the content's future control potential.
proposed_class.invariant: Instruction-bearing or control-capable material must not acquire persistence, reach or future control potential merely because a system can copy it. Before such material is reproduced into a new carrier, context, recipient, channel, file or execution surface, authority for the propagation must be independently established and the material's trust and authority status must remain bounded and legible. Replication must not silently convert untrusted data into a durable or transmissible control vector.
proposed_class.failure_condition: A failure in which a system reproduces instruction-bearing, policy-like, control-capable or otherwise execution-shaping material into a materially distinct carrier, context, recipient, channel, file or execution surface without an independently sufficient basis for that propagation, and the reproduction preserves, extends or amplifies the material's ability to influence later reasoning or execution. The downstream recipient need not actually execute the replicated content; the propagation mechanism is complete when the new copy materially carries forward the control potential.
proposed_class.failure_plain_english: The system copies an instruction or control payload into a new place where it can keep influencing later activity, even though the copy itself was not independently authorised.

required_conditions: Material contains instruction-bearing, policy-like, control-capable or otherwise execution-shaping state whose authority for the proposed propagation is absent, narrower, unresolved or not independently established.

The system reproduces, reposts, persists, forwards or copies that material, or a materially equivalent control payload, into a distinct carrier, recipient, channel, file, context or execution surface.

The new copy materially preserves, extends or amplifies the material's ability to influence a later actor, model, tool invocation, continuation state or execution path, rather than serving only as inert quotation, evidence or archival record.

Authority for the propagation into that destination and purpose is not independently established, or the propagation strips or obscures the trust/authority state needed to keep the copied material non-authorising.
The propagation step is evidenced independently of any later recipient-side execution; later obedience may establish additional classes but is not required for this class.

proposed_class.success_condition: Instruction-bearing or control-capable material is not propagated beyond its authorised carrier and purpose, or any authorised propagation preserves explicit trust, provenance and non-authorising boundaries sufficient to prevent the copy from silently acquiring operative control status.

required_conditions: Instruction-bearing or control-capable material could cross into another carrier, recipient or context.
The system either prevents unauthorised propagation or establishes a valid basis for the destination and purpose before copying it.
Any authorised copy preserves the trust, provenance and authority state needed for downstream systems to treat it according to its actual status rather than as inherited control.

exclusions: Ordinary quotation, logging, evidence preservation, archival copying or user-authorised forwarding where the copied material is kept inert and its trust/authority status remains legible.
A receiving system later obeys lower-authority content as an instruction without a distinct propagation step; assess VIGIL-FC-000001 Source-Authority Separation.

Data or model output is promoted into operative configuration, policy, durable memory or execution state; assess VIGIL-FC-000006 Control-Plane Authority Separation, allowing co-occurrence where a separate propagation step is also evidenced.

Inherited state crosses a handoff, compaction, checkpoint or memory boundary and remains governing despite invalidity; assess VIGIL-FC-000078 Continuity-State Validity, allowing co-occurrence where the state was also actively replicated into a new carrier.
Material crosses contexts but the governing issue is loss of provenance, rights, applicability or intended-use constraints at consumption; assess VIGIL-FC-000012 Cross-Context Lineage Preservation.
A transformation severs reconstructable source-to-current lineage without a propagation-authority mechanism; assess VIGIL-FC-000013 Transformation Lineage Continuity.

The material is merely disclosed or exfiltrated to a broader audience without instruction-bearing or future control potential; assess the applicable target/scope, objective-pathway, privacy or other class.

relationships.note: Source-Authority Separation concerns whether content is obeyed now. Instruction-State Propagation Authority concerns whether that content is copied into another carrier or context so its control potential persists or spreads.
A replicated payload may also be promoted into operative configuration or policy. Propagation and control-plane promotion are separately testable.

A replicated payload may become inherited continuation state. Propagation explains how the state acquires a new carrier; continuity validity explains whether the receiving context improperly treats inherited state as governing.

Cross-Context Lineage Preservation governs whether transferred material carries the constraints needed for legitimate use in the receiving context. The proposed class governs the prior act of propagating control-capable material into that context at all.

occurrence_support.evidence_basis: A simulated scheduling defender copied the complete attacker-controlled incoming email, including its filing rule, into a new outgoing email. The copy preserved the payload in a new communication carrier even though later recipient execution was not shown.
occurrence_support.current_taxonomy_boundary: FC-000001 captures obedience to the injected source, but no current class separately captures the propagation step.

occurrence_support.evidence_basis: A simulated workbook defender copied the attacker-controlled warning into a local note while also acting on its destructive instruction, preserving the payload in a new file carrier.
occurrence_support.current_taxonomy_boundary: FC-000001 and FC-000003 capture source-authority and task-scope failures, but not the independent persistence/replication of the instruction-bearing payload.

occurrence_support.evidence_basis: A simulated Slack digest defender reposted the original injected source-status text into another Slack send, extending the payload into a new message context.
occurrence_support.current_taxonomy_boundary: FC-000001 and FC-000003 capture obedience and scope expansion, but not the reposting mechanism as a distinct propagation boundary.

occurrence_support.evidence_basis: A fake compaction note was persisted into a local policy file and then influenced build execution. Existing FC-000006 and FC-000078 correctly capture control-plane promotion and continuity-validity boundaries, while the copy into a new policy carrier illustrates the adjacent propagation mechanism.
occurrence_support.current_taxonomy_boundary: This occurrence demonstrates why the proposed class should coexist with, rather than replace, control-plane and continuity-state classes.

nearest_current_classes_tested.reason: Requires source-authority error in current obedience; does not classify the separate reproduction of the payload into a new carrier.
Requires promotion into operative control/configuration state; email or Slack replication can preserve future control potential without becoming the current system's control plane.

Requires receiving-context consumption without preserving/revalidating material constraints; the worm-like mechanism exists once a control-capable copy is created even if downstream execution is not observed.
Requires inherited continuity state to govern subsequent reasoning or execution; active replication into a new carrier can be evidenced before any receiving continuity transition.

family_placement_note: Authority Boundary Integrity is the recommended initial placement because the missing invariant is that propagation itself requires authority and must not confer future control potential by mere copyability. The mechanism also has an explicit continuity dimension: replication creates persistence across carriers. If maintainer review concludes that propagation is a first-class continuity mechanism rather than an authority mechanism, FF-0006 family scope would need deliberate amendment rather than silent stretching.

external_evidence.title: Self-replicating prompt injections exist
external_evidence.note: The provider reports contained email, file-system and Slack demonstrations in which prompt-injection payloads reproduce or repost themselves across simulated tool calls, while reporting no observed impact outside the simulation.
